title: Latency scenario lab notes — week of 2026-11-28
body:
Purpose:
Quick capture of the latency-focused lab we ran this week: surface short-tail and long-tail contributors, verify that new sampling + adaptive-aggregation reduces storage and dashboard cost without losing signal at p95/p99, and iterate on a compact dashboard for pager/SE oncall use.

High-level summary:
- Ran two active experiments (A/B): adaptive-sampling v1 (ASv1) vs baseline (1:1 full traces for priority routes).
- Time window: 2026-11-24 00:00 -> 2026-11-27 23:59 (72h).
- Key routes: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings, hosted-internal ingest pipeline.
- Primary metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, end-to-end tail (client->response), host-side queue depth, KV-cache hit ratio, per-route trace size, telemetry storage bytes/day, and dashboard query cost estimate.

Experiment setup notes:
- Adaptive sampling rule: always capture 100% of errors, 20% of success flows by default, up to 80% for flows with >200ms deviation from route median. Implemented as a lightweight gateway hook (mateo/telemetry-proxy v0.9).
- Aggregation: new compaction step groups contiguous spans with identical tags (service, model-id, quantization-profile) within a 2s window to reduce span count.
- Retention: same 30d raw window, but compaction reduces effective storage and ingestion SLO.

Preliminary results (72h):
- Storage ingestion: baseline ~1.8TB/day; ASv1 ~680GB/day (≈62% reduction).
- Dashboard query cost (sampled queries measured): median query CPU down 48%, avg scan rows down 55% on ad-hoc traces panel.
- Latency metrics: p50 unchanged; p95 increased by +6ms on /v1/generate (from 132ms to 138ms); p99 +12ms (from 312ms to 324ms).
- Alert fidelity: error-rate alerts unchanged; custom regression detection (prompt-variance detector) triggered 1 fewer false positive during noisy period.
- Signal loss: small: rare micro-patterns (multi-segment retries across model fallback path) were under-sampled and harder to reconstruct. We can reproduce on-demand by toggling debug-capture for those hashes.

Dashboard & UX changes proposed:
- New compact "Oncall Trace Snapshot" widget: single-row per route showing p50/p95/p99, last 24h trend sparkline, and a quick-link to a sampled golden-trace (opens debug dump). Aim: one-screen triage for SEs.
- Add an "Adaptive Sampling status" badge per route showing current effective sampling ratio and recent changes.
- Cost telemetry: new baked-in field in trace index: estimated-ingest-bytes and estimated-query-cost (micro-estimates used for budgeting).

Open issues / questions:
- Which routes legally require 100% tracing for compliance? (need input from security/compliance)
- How to decide offline whether a missed micro-pattern is acceptable vs needs retention? Proposal: maintain a sliding "replay buffer" (7d) for under-sampled hash families. Storage/ops cost TBD.
- Is the compaction heuristic (2s window + identical tags) too aggressive for multi-model chains? We observed one case where compaction removed timing boundaries that aid diagnosing re-quantization stalls.

Action items / owners:
- (Mateo) add toggle for debug-capture by trace-hash and wire a lightweight retention flag; target: PoC by 2026-12-05.
- (Sofia) mockups for Oncall Trace Snapshot and Adaptive Sampling badge; sync with product-hosted-api for placement in console; due 2026-12-02.
- (Ravi) run a follow-up ASv1 run but with compaction window reduced to 500ms for multi-model routes; collect 72h metrics; start 2026-12-01.
- (Ava) file a short note to security/compliance: need list of routes with 100% retention requirement; ping by 2026-11-30.

Meeting notes (standup 2026-11-28):
- Quick sync: Mateo walked through proxy hook and initial perf numbers.
- Sofia demoed dashboard mockups; early feedback: oncall wants a one-click copy of trace link for Slack.
- Ravi called out a regression in the compaction pipeline that surfaced in ci-load test; mitigation: switch to staged compaction (apply to 10% traffic first).
- Decisions: proceed to staged rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) after the 500ms compaction test.

Short-term risks:
- Under-sampling multi-segment retries may delay root-cause for complex degradations (low-medium risk).
- Cost-model variance: current ingest estimate uses historical averages — sudden model churn could change per-trace size; add a daily recalibration job.

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep a small list of sample trace-ids to repro the missing micro-patterns (saved in /tmp/trace-repros.txt).
- When filing follow-ups, include a tiny GIF of dashboard animation to reduce miscommunication.

Relevant links (internal):
- Telemetry proxy PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/312
- Dashboard mockups (figma): https://www.figma.com/file/xxx/oncall-trace-snapshot
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-6421 (adaptive sampling rollout)

If you want to dig into raw numbers I have the raw csvs in google sheet: linked in Jira comment. Planning a short retro next Wednesday to decide whether to push ASv1 to canary on dedicated pools.

-- Ava
